<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIX.|OF THE APOSTLES.|349}}</noinclude>about the way of our Lord. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=24}}† For one named Demetrius, a siluersmith, that made siluer {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The Protestants translate, ''shrines'', in the bible an. 1577: to make the people thinke that it toucheth the holy ''shrines'' of Sainctes: most corruptly, the greeke signifying plainly, ''temples'', and that of heathē gods.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ναοὺς.''}}∷ temples of Diána, procured to the artificers no smal gaine: {{verse|chapter=19|verse=25}}† whom calling together and them that were the same kinde of workemen, he said, Sirs, you know that our gaine is of this occupation: {{verse|chapter=19|verse=26}}† and you see, and heare that this same Paul by persuasion hath auerted a great multitude not only of Ephesus, but almost of al Asia, saying, That they are not gods vvhich be made by handes. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=27}}† And not only vnto vs is this part in danger to be reproued, but also the temple of great Diana shal be reputed for nothing, yea & her maiestie shal begin to be destroied, vvhom al Asia & the vvorld worshippeth. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=28}}† Hearing these things, they were replenished with anger, and cried out saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=29}}† And the vvhole citie vvas filled vvith confusion, & they ranne violently vvith one accord into the theátre, catching Gaius and Aristarchus Macedonians, Paules companions. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=30}}† And vvhen Paul vvould haue entred in to the people, the disciples did not permit him. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=31}}† And certaine also of the Princes of Asia that vvere his frendes, sent vnto him, desyring that he vvould not aduenture him self into the theátre: {{verse|chapter=19|verse=32}}† and others cried an other thing. For the assemblie vvas confuse, & the more part knevv not for what cause they were assembled. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=33}}† And of the multitude they drevv forth Alexander, the Ievves thrusting him forvvard. But Alexander vvith his hand desiring silence, vvould haue giuen the people satisfaction. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=34}}† Vvhom as soone as they perceiued to be a Iewe, there vvas made one voice of al, almost for the space of tvvo houres crying out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=35}}† And when the Scribe had appeased the multitudes, he saith, Ye men of Ephesus, for vvhat man is there that knovveth not the citie of the Ephesians to be a vvorshipper of great Diana, & {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here the Heretikes adde to the text this word, ''image'', more then is in the greeke, to put a scruple into the peoples minde concerning holy ''Images''.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''τοῦ διοπετοῦς.''}}∷ Iupiters childe? {{verse|chapter=19|verse=36}}† Forasmuch therfore as these things can not be gainsaid, you must be quieted, and doe nothing rashly. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=37}}† For you haue brought these men, being neither sacrilegious, nor blaspheming your Goddesse. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=38}}† But if Demetrius and the artificers that are vvith him, haue matter to say against any man, there are Courtes kept in the common place, & there are Proconsuls, let them accuse one an other. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=39}}† And if you aske any other matter: it may be resolued in a lavvful assemblie. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=40}}† For we are in danger also to be accused for this daies sedition:<noinclude>{{rh||Xx iij|vvhereas}}</noinclude>
